title: Brand assets — implementation review
lede: Resources now has a separate, Google Drive-style Brand assets library for logos, fonts, reference files, templates, and the viewable brand-guide PDF. The library keeps one stable file row while each replacement becomes an immutable version.

stats.n: Vercel Blob stores private binaries; Prisma/Neon stores folders, file identity, versions, and upload intents
The current pointer advances to the next version; earlier files remain available
The current Preview PDF was uploaded explicitly during testing; migrations create no content

changesNote: The source implementation is supplemented by a clean authenticated desktop check and a side-by-side comparison with the supplied Google Drive reference. The review is intentionally presented as reference comparison plus runtime evidence rather than a matched before/after pair: the V1 component was untracked in the starting worktree, so a trustworthy same-product baseline capture is unavailable.

changes.was: The existing Resources page handled Markdown guides and supporting references, but had no durable file-library boundary for brand binaries.
changes.now: A URL-backed Brand assets tab isolates folders, file metadata, current versions, History, PDF viewing, and downloads without changing guide filters or Markdown semantics.

changes.h: Replacing a file would lose continuity
changes.was: A simple upload/delete workflow would force people to manage duplicate names and would remove the prior file from the product record.
changes.now: A stable logical file is unique within its folder. Uploading a new version advances an explicit current pointer and preserves the previous version in authenticated History.

changes.h: Large binaries need a storage boundary
changes.was: Routing a roughly 21.7 MB guide through a small server form upload would add unnecessary transport and timeout pressure, while a public URL would weaken access control.
changes.now: The client uses @vercel/blob/client with a short-lived actor-bound intent; the dedicated private store is read through an authenticated app proxy with no raw Blob URL returned.

changes.h: The first file-library layout was too dense
changes.was: The Brand assets surface repeated the same context across a large intro card, separate controls, recent cards, folder cards, and file cards with many always-visible actions.
changes.now: The surface now follows a Drive-style hierarchy: folder rail, working New/Home/Recent/Starred navigation, breadcrumb, one compact toolbar, suggested-folder tiles, and a unified table with secondary actions behind the row menu.

verification: Focused asset tests: 26 tests pass for name/type/size validation, the original V1 contracts, and the approved experience contracts.

Repository gates: npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false, full npm run lint, npx prisma validate, npm run db:migrate:check, npm run build:app, npm run codemap, npm run verify:docs, and git diff --check pass.
Build route proof: the optimized build includes /resources plus all Brand assets list, folder, upload-token, completion, detail, download, favorite, and restore routes.

Full suite: 3,890 tests pass and 9 fail in 7 unrelated existing files (Welcome, Schedule timeline, Snow Leopard, operational target baseline, two kiosk hardening suites, and hidden-user visibility); clean-checkout reproduction was not run because the worktree already contains parallel changes.

Runtime proof: a fresh authenticated Admin browser tab reached /resources?tab=brand-assets at desktop, rendered the uploaded PDF in the unified table, opened and closed the compact New, Filters, and row-action menus, switched Recent/Starred/Home views, observed 200 responses for the asset-list and PDF download routes, and recorded zero browser console errors. The browser capture is saved as brand-assets-drive-after.jpg.

Migration/read-back: Preview migration health passed with 141/141 local migrations applied and no pending or failed rows. The earlier provisioning read-back confirmed one technical root and no seeded content; current Preview contains one explicitly uploaded PDF for lifecycle testing.
notes: The supplied PDF was explicitly uploaded through the authenticated UI and its list/download/preview route read-back passed. Upload one replacement and confirm both versions plus audit rows read back.

A matched same-product before/after UI capture remains deferred because the component was untracked at the start of this pass; the supplied Google Drive screenshot is used as a structural reference, not mislabeled as a product baseline.
No initial folders, files, or PDF are required. The migration creates only the empty technical root container so users can create their own organization.
